solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dutiful detectives in a Vauxhall plant?

indicators.note: in tells us the earlier words sit inside the car named after them

parts.note: the Astra is a model of Vauxhall car
PI is the standard short form of pious, which is dutiful
DIs are detective inspectors

explanation.surface: A question about some conscientious police officers stationed at a Vauxhall car factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a car works, but it is the definition: a potted house plant. Vauxhall is a British car maker.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspidistra is a hardy leafy houseplant, famously a fixture of Victorian and Edwardian parlours.

clue.text: Marksman at distance up on legs

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: re means on or concerning
pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: A rifleman far away stands up on his own two feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper is a marksman who shoots at targets from a concealed spot a long way off.

clue.text: Eliot's nephew out to assess old writer: 24 5 22 26

indicators.note: out suggests the words are put out of their order, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words, without the apostrophe
to eye something is to look it over and assess it
O is the usual abbreviation for old
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Some relative of the poet Eliot is out to evaluate an old author.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference: the answers to 24, 5, 22 and 26 read REMAIN VIGILANT AT ALL TIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: To sleep with one eye open is an idiom for staying on guard even while resting, i.e. keeping watch constantly.

clue.text: Clean standing stone in rush

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to rub something can clean it
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: Instructions to scrub an upright megalith quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone in British weight is 14 pounds, abbreviated st.
explanation.definitionFit: To burst in or out is to rush suddenly, as in bursting into a room.

clue.text: Six humongous guards left on watch

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: something that guards another keeps it enclosed within it

parts.note: giant as an adjective means huge
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Half a dozen enormous sentries stand guard, alert to everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Being vigilant means staying alert for danger, which is what someone on watch must be.

clue.text: Put stop to drink in Irish city

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to seal a bottle with a stopper
second meaning: the city in the south of Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone stops drinking while visiting a city in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like going teetotal; the first meaning is literal, stoppering the drink's bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to plug a bottle, and it is also the name of Ireland's second city.

clue.text: Country roads run back past a club

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back means the words before it are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: lanes are narrow country roads
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone runs back along rural roads, past a club building.
explanation.walkthrough: Past places the reversed roads-and-run after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a famous North London football club.

clue.text: Ship journey south in a line

indicators.note: in tells us the journey and direction sit inside the line

parts.note: taken as written
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line
to go is to journey
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A ship sails south in single file.
explanation.definitionFit: An argosy is a large merchant ship, originally from Ragusa, in poetic and old usage.

clue.text: Fabulous animal rook in college study

parts.note: uni is short for university

indicators.note: in tells us the chess piece sits inside the study

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A legendary beast, or a chess rook, spotted in a college study.
explanation.walkthrough: Fabulous here means of fable, not marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: The unicorn is a mythical creature of legend, a beast found only in fables.

clue.text: Without clothing in fresh air did you say?

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for the noun: the state of being without clothing

indicators.note: asking what was said points to how the words sound when spoken

parts.note: fresh means new
an air is a tune, a ditty

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you went out naked into the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh air' reads as one phrase but splits into two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudity is the condition of being naked, wearing nothing at all.

clue.text: Dread losing loud musical talent

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: fear is dread
f is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A musician's stage fright costs them their gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Having an ear for music means having a natural ability to recognise and reproduce it.

clue.text: Look relaxed in G&S role at last

indicators.note: in tells us the relaxed word sits between the two letters of the operetta pair

parts.note: the letters of Gilbert and Sullivan's initials
limp means slack or relaxed

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of role

explanation.surface: An actor looks laid-back playing a part in a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta.
explanation.walkthrough: G&S is Gilbert and Sullivan, the Victorian comic opera partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: A glimpse is a brief look, a quick sight of something.

clue.text: Riled member unable to stand by Irish king

parts.note: IR is the abbreviation for Irish
K is the chess notation for king
ED is erectile dysfunction, a cheeky reading of a member that cannot stand up

explanation.surface: An angry legislator, too lame to rise, sits next to a king of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The member looks like an MP or a limb, but it is a bawdy joke: ED, erectile dysfunction, comes after the Irish king.
explanation.definitionFit: Irked is a synonym of annoyed or vexed, the same as riled.

clue.text: Piano not in time backed viola part

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for soft

indicators.note: backed means the word before it is run in the opposite direction

parts.note: arriving late is not being in time

explanation.surface: A pianist out of time accompanies a viola player's part.
explanation.walkthrough: The viola here is not the instrument but the flower, the genus that includes pansies.
explanation.definitionFit: A petal is one of the coloured leaf-like sections of a flower such as the viola.

clue.text: Princess in factory returning poor parts

indicators.note: returning means the combined letters are read the way they came, backwards
in tells us the princess sits inside the factory

parts.note: a works is a factory
Di is Princess Diana

explanation.surface: A princess goes back to the factory in a deprived area.
explanation.definitionFit: Skid row is the run-down district of a city where the destitute live, so poor parts of town.

clue.text: First-class trotter perhaps for cooking?

parts.note: A as in A1, first-class
a trotter is a pig's foot

explanation.surface: A top-quality pig's trotter is offered for the cooking pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking' looks like the kitchen sense of the trotter but means happening, as in 'what's cooking?'
explanation.definitionFit: Something afoot is in preparation or going on, which is the idiomatic sense of 'cooking'.

clue.text: See 3
Arrange meets involving intimate community

indicators.note: involving means wrapping around the next word
to arrange is to set things in a new order, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters of meets
cosy means intimate and snug

explanation.surface: Organise gatherings that bring a close-knit community together.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecosystem is a biological community of organisms interacting with their environment.

clue.text: Credit to English on strategic move in game

parts.note: buying on tick means buying on credit
a tack is a course of action
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A tactical play is credited to an English side in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'to English on strategic move' puts the TO E after the move.
explanation.definitionFit: Tick-tack-toe is a variant spelling of tic-tac-toe, the American name for noughts and crosses.

clue.text: Unexpected buzz from Parky's visit?

parts.note: parky is British slang for chilly
to pay a call is to visit

explanation.surface: A surprise phone call from the TV chat-show host Parkinson, known as Parky.
explanation.walkthrough: Parky looks like Michael Parkinson's nickname, but it is the adjective, slang for cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold call is an unsolicited sales phone call, a buzz nobody was expecting.

clue.text: Fermented grapes and cheap cigarette

indicators.note: fermenting changes something chemically, so the letters are transformed

parts.note: the letters of grapes

explanation.surface: Cheap wine and a cheap smoke: a modest night in.
explanation.walkthrough: Gasper is old British slang for a cheap cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasper is slang for a cheap, harsh cigarette, named for the effect on the smoker.

clue.text: Commercial demands at first frustrate nurses

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold something close, so one part is held inside another

parts.note: to avert a plan is to frustrate or prevent it

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of demands

explanation.surface: Commercial demands thwart the nurses at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' looks like a noun for hospital staff, but it is the verb, holding the letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An advert is a commercial, a short promotional message in print or on air.

clue.text: Fully accepting thanks for any reason?

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase that fits questions such as 'why at all?'

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: all means fully, as in all alone
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone graciously accepts thanks but wonders why they were offered.
explanation.definitionFit: At all intensifies questions and negatives, so 'why at all?' asks whether there is any reason whatever.

clue.text: Arrested Romeo's inside: fell from grace

indicators.note: inside tells us the letter sits within the other word

parts.note: to arrest a process is to stay or halt it
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo is detained in custody, having fallen from grace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrested' suggests a police matter; it means halted, as in stayed proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to wander from the right moral path, so strayed means fell from grace.

clue.text: Old woman in control to persist

indicators.note: in tells us the woman sits inside the control

parts.note: a rein is a means of control
old woman is slang for mother, ma

explanation.surface: An elderly lady in charge refuses to give up.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain is to continue existing or carry on, which is to persist.

clue.text: Spotted cuckoo

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a birdwatcher's sighting; both words are adjectives instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means dotted all over, and is also informal for mildly mad or eccentric.

clue.text: Bond's keeping millions by

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one part goes inside

parts.note: ties are bonds
M is the abbreviation for millions

explanation.surface: James Bond is holding on to millions nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond's' is read as bonds, plural, rather than belonging to 007.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic, times means multiplied by, as in three times four.

clue.text: Wordplay one contrived initially in old tongue

parts.note: a pun is a piece of wordplay
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of contrived

explanation.surface: A forced joke appears in an ancient language.
explanation.definitionFit: Punic is the extinct language of ancient Carthage, a Phoenician dialect.

clue.text: Northern wood for designer John

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
ash is a kind of timber

explanation.surface: Northern timber chosen for a designer's project.
explanation.definitionFit: John Nash was the Regency architect who designed Regent Street and Brighton Pavilion.

clue.text: Celeb very like Neo using MDMA

parts.note: so means very
Neo is the setter, so from his point of view this is me
on as in on drugs, using them
E is ecstasy, the drug MDMA

explanation.surface: A celebrity much like the setter is taking ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Neo is the setter, so 'like Neo' gives the first-person pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A someone is a person of importance or fame, the opposite of a nobody.

clue.text: Satisfied with Rowley's force?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the police force headed by Sir Mark Rowley

explanation.walkthrough: Sir Mark Rowley is Commissioner of London's Metropolitan Police; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of meet works as 'satisfied' for requirements, and the Met is the Metropolitan Police.

clue.text: Decide to crack clues again

parts.note: re- is the prefix for again
to crack clues is to solve them

explanation.surface: A solver decides to attack the puzzle once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve is to make a firm decision to do something.

clue.text: Plain endive cooked twice for starter

indicators.note: cooking changes ingredients, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters of endive

indicators.note: a starter comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of twice

explanation.surface: A menu note: endive, cooked two ways, served as the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like a description of the dish; it is the definition, meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident means clearly seen or understood, the same as plain in the sense of obvious.
